title: Three Pounds of Argument
subtitle: 生命科学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）
meta: 主题语境：生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）　|　核心词汇：brain　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 brain 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my mother was sent to weigh ① a brain she could not name, and she said the naming was the whole of the lesson. The ② brain, meaning the organ and not the mind, was three pounds and was carried by whoever came last; a brain, she said, is the only thing in a laboratory that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ brain in that jar had the same label, and the ④ brain at the front, meaning the one the surgeon held and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever weighed properly. A brain, my grandmother said, is nine parts water and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the water is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ brain was the whole of the person, meaning the mind and not the organ. The ⑥ brain, meaning the mind and not any of that, is the only thing in a family that everybody praises and nobody questions; a brain, he said, is either something you weigh or the only word that means both an organ and a mind. She said the mind is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ brain had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the water. The ⑧ brain of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was three pounds of organ and eleven years of weighing; a brain, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ brain I remember is the one at the front, which was drawn in 1979 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ brain, my grandmother said in 1984, is the only thing that improves by being used; every brain, she said, is a mind that has agreed to look like an organ. She said the mind was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 脑（指器官本身，与心智相对）
C. 固定搭配：weigh a brain 称一个脑的重量
D. n. 脑（指罐子里每一个）
E. n. 脑（指前面那一个）
F. n. 脑力；心智（抽象：与器官相对）
G. n. 那份心智（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a brain she could not name
The brain, meaning the organ and not the mind
brain was the whole of the person
the brain had become a number in a report
The brain of the whole thing
A brain, my grandmother said in 1984

answers.why: weigh a brain 意为“称一个脑的重量”，1958 年母亲被派去称一个她说不出名字的脑。
brain 意为“脑”，指器官本身而不是心智，重三磅，由最后走的人拿着。
brain 指罐子里每一个脑，每一个都是同样的标签。
brain 指前面那一个（外科医生拿的那一个），是唯一有人认真称过的。
brain 意为“脑力、心智”，与器官相对，父亲说 brain 就是那个人的全部。
brain 为抽象用法，指那份心智本身，是一家人里人人都夸、却没人质疑的东西。
brain 意为“脑、大脑”，到 1974 年这个 brain 成了报告里的一个数字。
brain 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是三磅的器官和十一年的称量。
brain 意为“脑”，我记得的是前面那一个，1979 年被画下来，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
brain 为抽象总称，祖母说大脑是唯一会因为被使用而变好的东西。
